subject: Biology
prompt: Mosaic egg cleavage pattern is seen in which phylum?
explain: Annelida shows spiral & mosaic (determinate) cleavage; fate of cells is fixed from early cleavage.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which Echinoderm can regenerate a complete body from one arm?
explain: Brittle stars (Ophiura) show remarkable regeneration; some can regrow whole body from a single arm.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Aves (birds) is now extinct?
explain: Archaeopteryx is an extinct connecting link between reptiles & birds; fossil shows both characters.

subject: Biology
prompt: Pedal glands secreting byssus threads for attachment are seen in:
explain: Mytilus (marine mussel) secretes byssus threads from pedal gland to anchor itself to substrate.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which larval stage of Echinodermata is bilaterally symmetrical?
explain: Bipinnaria (starfish larva) is bilaterally symmetrical; adult starfish show radial symmetry.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Arthropoda has antennae TWO pairs & millipedes as examples?
explain: Millipedes (Diplopoda/Myriapoda) have 2 pairs of antennae and 2 pairs of legs per segment.

subject: Biology
prompt: Peripatus is a connecting link between Annelida & Arthropoda. It belongs to:
explain: Peripatus (velvet worm) of phylum Onychophora shows characters of both Annelida and Arthropoda.

subject: Biology
prompt: Diphycercal tail (symmetrical, with notochord extending to tip) is seen in:
explain: Lungfish (Dipnoi) have diphycercal tail; heterocercal tail is in sharks; homocercal in bony fish.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is the correct NCERT example of class Reptilia (Squamata—snakes)?
explain: Naja (cobra) is a snake (Serpentes/Squamata). NCERT lists Naja as reptile example.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which animal shows torsion (twisting of visceral mass 180°) during development?
explain: Torsion is unique to class Gastropoda of Mollusca; it repositions mantle cavity to the front.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has organisms with a lophophore feeding organ?
explain: Lophophore is a horseshoe-shaped ciliated feeding organ found in Brachiopoda & Phoronida (minor coelomate phyla).

subject: Biology
prompt: Hemichordates have which structure homologous to notochord?
explain: Balanoglossus has a stomochord (buccal diverticulum) in the proboscis, considered homologous to the chordate notochord.
